title: JRE 2364 - Brandon Epstein
guestBio: Brandon Epstein is a mental performance coach, speaker, and author of several books, the most recent of which is "The Success Code: "Programmed to Fail: How to Break Through Your Mental Block and Achieve Greatness."
tldr: Brandon Epstein discusses mental performance coaching and breaking through psychological barriers to achieve success
The conversation explores how people are 'programmed to fail' through limiting beliefs and negative mental patterns
Epstein shares strategies for reprogramming the mind and overcoming self-imposed mental blocks
Discussion of how mental performance applies to various fields including business, sports, and personal development
The importance of understanding your mental programming and how it shapes your reality and outcomes
Practical techniques for shifting mindset and achieving peak performance in competitive situations
recap:
Joe Rogan sits down with mental performance coach Brandon Epstein on JRE 2364 to dive into the psychology of success and the invisible barriers that hold people back. Epstein has built a career helping people understand why they sabotage themselves and how to break through those mental limitations. The core of his message centers on the idea that most people are literally programmed to fail through years of conditioning, negative self-talk, and limiting beliefs picked up from family, society, and past experiences.

The conversation gets into how your mental programming operates like software running in the background of your consciousness. You might consciously want success, but if your subconscious programming says you don't deserve it or you're not capable of it, that deeper programming wins every time. Epstein breaks down how peak performers across different fields share common traits when it comes to mental discipline and the ability to reprogram themselves. Joe and Brandon discuss real examples of how this plays out, from athletes choking under pressure to entrepreneurs self-sabotaging their businesses right when they're about to break through.

Epstein's book The Success Code: Programmed to Fail lays out a framework for identifying where your mental programming is limiting you and provides actionable steps to reprogram those patterns. The discussion touches on visualization, self-talk, understanding your triggers, and creating new neural pathways through repetition and conscious practice. It's not about positive thinking or ignoring real obstacles, but rather getting brutally honest about what beliefs are actually driving your behavior and choices.

Roe brings up how this applies to combat sports and competition, which resonates with Epstein's experience working with high-level performers. The mental game is often the difference between winning and losing at elite levels. They explore how fear and doubt are actually just neural patterns that can be retrained, and how most limitations are self-imposed rather than real. The conversation emphasizes that this work is uncomfortable because it requires looking at yourself honestly and being willing to change patterns that have been deeply ingrained for years.
